content_voiceover: This algorithm outlines management of grade one to two follicular lymphoma based on stage and tumor burden. For limited stage disease, options include involved-site radiotherapy, anti-CD20 therapy with or without radiation, or immunochemotherapy with or without radiation. For advanced stage, stage two bulky, or B-symptomatic disease, the next branch point is tumor burden. Asymptomatic patients with low tumor burden can be managed with watchful waiting or immediate rituximab, since studies show no survival difference between the two approaches, though watch and wait avoids unnecessary treatment toxicity. Symptomatic patients with high tumor burden require active treatment. Tumor burden itself is defined by the GELF criteria, which the table lists, any nodal or extranodal mass greater than seven centimeters, three or more nodal sites larger than three centimeters, elevated LDH, hemoglobin under ten, absolute neutrophil count under one point five, platelets under one hundred, splenomegaly greater than sixteen centimeters by CT, risk of organ compression, or significant serous effusions. Knowing these criteria helps decide who needs treatment versus who can be safely observed.
keypoints: Limited stage: involved-site RT, anti-CD20, or immunochemotherapy
Advanced stage guided by symptoms and tumor burden
Low burden, asymptomatic: watch and wait or immediate rituximab
High burden or symptomatic disease requires active treatment
GELF criteria define high tumor burden
keypoint_voiceover: For limited stage follicular lymphoma, treat with radiotherapy or anti-CD20-based therapy. For advanced disease, asymptomatic low tumor burden patients can be watched or given rituximab alone, while symptomatic high tumor burden patients need active treatment. High tumor burden is defined by the GELF criteria, covering large masses, multiple nodal sites, elevated LDH, cytopenias, splenomegaly, organ compression, or effusions.
